provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Electoral systems
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain different electoral systems
The students should be able to compare major electoral systems
The students should be able to identify electoral systems used in Nigeria

Introduction:
We have previously studied the structure of government in Nigeria. Today we will examine how citizens choose their representatives through different electoral systems.

Content:
Electoral systems are the methods used to conduct elections and allocate seats in legislative bodies. The major types include first-past-the-post, proportional representation, and mixed systems. First-past-the-post, used in Nigeria, awards seats to candidates with the highest votes in each constituency. Proportional representation allocates seats based on vote share across regions. The electoral commission in Nigeria, INEC, conducts elections using these systems. For example, during the 2023 presidential election, the winner needed the highest number of votes and over 25% in at least 24 states.

Class activity:
Students will be divided into groups to simulate different electoral systems using class monitor elections as a case study.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is an electoral system?
2. Differentiate between first-past-the-post and proportional representation
3. Why is a simple majority important in Nigerian elections?
4. How does INEC ensure free and fair elections?

Summary:
Electoral systems determine how votes are translated into representation in government.

topics.title: Public opinion
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define public opinion
The students should be able to explain how public opinion is formed
The students should be able to identify methods of measuring public opinion

Introduction:
Following our study of political participation, we now examine how collective views on issues shape governance.

Content:
Public opinion refers to the collective attitudes and views held by citizens on political issues and leaders. It is formed through various channels including family, education, media, and religious institutions. In Nigeria, public opinion is strongly influenced by religious leaders, traditional rulers, and social media platforms. Measuring public opinion can be done through polls, surveys, and analysis of public discourse. For example, during the fuel subsidy removal debate, public opinion was measured through street interviews and social media sentiment analysis.

Class activity:
Students will conduct a simple survey on a current political issue and present their findings.

Evaluation questions:
1. Define public opinion
2. List three factors that influence public opinion in Nigeria
3. How is public opinion measured in a developing country like Nigeria?
4. Why is public opinion important to democratic governance?

Summary:
Public opinion serves as a critical check on government power and influences policy decisions.

topics.title: Pressure groups
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different types of pressure groups
The students should be able to explain tactics used by pressure groups
The students should be able to evaluate the effectiveness of pressure groups in Nigeria

Introduction:
After studying political parties, we now examine organized groups that influence government decisions without seeking political power.

Content:
Pressure groups are organized associations that seek to influence government policies without contesting elections. They can be classified as sectional (representing specific interests like NUPENG) or promotional (seeking general goals like environmental protection). Common tactics used include lobbying, protests, strikes, and public campaigns. In Nigeria, pressure groups like the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and civil society organizations play significant roles in governance. For instance, during the #EndSARS protests, young Nigerians organized through social media to demand police reform.

Class activity:
Students will research a Nigerian pressure group and present its objectives and tactics to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. Differentiate between sectional and promotional pressure groups
2. List three tactics used by pressure groups in Nigeria
3. How do pressure groups complement the work of political parties?
4. Evaluate the impact of pressure groups on Nigerian democracy

Summary:
Pressure groups provide alternative channels for citizen participation in the political process.

topics.title: Civil service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to describe the structure of Nigerian civil service
The students should be able to explain the role of civil service in governance
The students should be able to identify challenges facing the civil service

Introduction:
Having studied the executive arm of government, we now examine the permanent bureaucracy that implements government policies.

Content:
The Nigerian civil service is the administrative machinery of government responsible for implementing policies. It is structured into federal, state, and local government levels. At the federal level, it is headed by the Head of Civil Service, with ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs) handling specific functions. The civil service performs crucial roles including policy formulation, implementation, and advisory services to the government. Challenges facing the civil service include bureaucracy, corruption, and inadequate funding. For example, the slow processing of passports in the immigration service reflects bureaucratic inefficiency.

Class activity:
Students will create an organizational chart showing the structure of a typical Nigerian ministry.

Evaluation questions:
1. Describe the structure of Nigerian civil service
2. Explain the roles of civil servants in policy implementation
3. Identify three challenges facing the civil service in Nigeria
4. How can the civil service be made more efficient?

Summary:
The civil service serves as the backbone of governance by translating policies into actionable programs.

topics.title: Local government
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the functions of local government
The students should be able to identify key reforms in local government administration
The students should be able to evaluate the effectiveness of local governments in Nigeria

Introduction:
After studying the federal structure of government, we focus on the third tier of government closest to the people.

Content:
Local government is the third tier of government in Nigeria, established to bring governance closer to the people. Its functions include providing services like primary education, healthcare, waste management, and maintaining local infrastructure. Key reforms include the 1976 local government reform that created a uniform system nationwide and the 2014 amendment that increased financial autonomy. Despite these reforms, local governments face challenges including inadequate funding, excessive control by state governments, and corruption. For example, many local councils struggle to maintain roads and markets due to limited resources.

Class activity:
Students will debate whether local governments should be granted more financial autonomy.

Evaluation questions:
1. List five functions of local government in Nigeria
2. Explain the significance of the 1976 local government reform
3. Identify three challenges facing local government administration
4. How can local governments be made more effective in service delivery?

Summary:
Local government serves as a vital link between the government and the people at the grassroots level.

topics.title: Military in politics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain how military coups occur
The students should be able to identify reasons for military intervention in politics
The students should be able to evaluate the impact of military rule in Nigeria

Introduction:
Following our study of constitutional governance, we examine periods when the military assumed political power in Nigeria.

Content:
The military has intervened in Nigerian politics through coups d'état, which are sudden seizures of government by military officers. Reasons for military intervention include political instability, corruption, and ethnic tensions. In Nigeria's history, military rule occurred from 1966-1979 and 1983-1999. During these periods, the military governed through decrees, suspended the constitution, and dissolved democratic institutions. The impact of military rule includes the centralization of power, suppression of civil liberties, and retardation of democratic development. For example, the Buhari/Idiagbon regime (1983-1985) introduced the War Against Indiscipline (WAI) campaign.

Class activity:
Students will create a timeline of military coups in Nigeria and their immediate outcomes.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the process of a military coup
2. Identify three reasons for military intervention in Nigerian politics
3. Compare civilian and military rule in Nigeria
4. How did military rule affect Nigeria's democratic development?

Summary:
Military intervention in politics disrupts democratic governance and has long-term consequences for nation-building.

topics.title: Foreign policy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain Nigeria's foreign policy objectives
The students should be able to identify principles guiding Nigeria's foreign policy
The students should be able to evaluate Nigeria's role in international relations

Introduction:
After studying domestic governance, we now examine Nigeria's relations with other countries and international organizations.

Content:
Nigeria's foreign policy is guided by principles including African unity, non-alignment, and peaceful coexistence. Key objectives include promoting regional integration, protecting national interests, and contributing to global peace. Nigeria has played significant roles in international organizations such as the United Nations, African Union, and ECOWAS. For example, Nigeria contributed troops to peacekeeping missions in Sierra Leone and Liberia during the 1990s. Under the principle of Afrocentrism, Nigeria has championed the African cause in international forums, supporting liberation movements during the apartheid era in South Africa.

Class activity:
Students will role-play a diplomatic negotiation between Nigeria and another country on a current issue.

Evaluation questions:
1. List three principles guiding Nigeria's foreign policy
2. Explain the principle of Afrocentrism in Nigeria's foreign policy
3. Identify two major achievements of Nigeria in international relations
4. How has Nigeria's foreign policy evolved since independence?

Summary:
Nigeria's foreign policy reflects its aspiration to be a leader in Africa and a respected voice in global affairs.

topics.title: International organisations
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the structure and functions of the UN
The students should be able to identify Nigeria's role in the AU and ECOWAS
The students should be able to evaluate the effectiveness of international organizations

Introduction:
Building on our study of foreign policy, we examine key international organizations that shape global governance.

Content:
The United Nations (UN) is the most universal international organization, established in 1945 to maintain peace and security. It has six principal organs including the General Assembly and Security Council. The African Union (AU) replaced the OAU in 2002, focusing on political and economic integration. ECOWAS, established in 1975, promotes economic cooperation and conflict resolution in West Africa. Nigeria plays significant roles in these organizations, contributing troops to peacekeeping missions and hosting ECOWAS meetings. For example, Nigeria has been a major contributor to ECOWAS peacekeeping forces in The Gambia.

Class activity:
Students will research and present on Nigeria's contributions to one international organization.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the structure of the United Nations
2. Identify three objectives of the African Union
3. How does ECOWAS contribute to regional integration in West Africa?
4. Evaluate Nigeria's role in international organizations

Summary:
International organizations provide platforms for cooperation and collective action on global issues.

topics.title: Mock paper one
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to apply knowledge of government concepts to exam questions
The students should be able to manage time effectively during examinations
The students should be able to demonstrate proper examination techniques

Introduction:
As we approach the final examinations, we will practice with a mock paper to assess our preparedness.

Content:
Today we will complete a full mock paper one examination covering topics from the term. The paper will include multiple-choice questions, short answer questions, and essay questions similar to WAEC standard. Students should allocate time wisely, spending approximately 40 minutes on section A, 30 minutes on section B, and 50 minutes on section C. Proper examination techniques include reading questions carefully, planning answers before writing, and managing time effectively. For example, when answering an essay question on pressure groups, students should provide definitions, types, and examples with proper referencing.

Class activity:
Students will complete the full mock paper under timed conditions.

Evaluation questions:
The mock paper itself serves as evaluation with questions covering all topics studied this term.

Summary:
The mock examination helps identify areas needing improvement before the final exams.

topics.title: Revision and WAEC practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall key concepts from the term's topics
The students should be able to answer WAEC-style questions accurately
The students should be able to identify common mistakes in government examinations

Introduction:
Having completed our mock examination, we now focus on targeted revision and practice with past WAEC questions.

Content:
Revision involves systematically reviewing all topics covered this term with emphasis on areas identified as challenging. WAEC past papers provide insight into examination patterns, question formats, and marking schemes. Students should practice answering questions under timed conditions to improve speed and accuracy. Common mistakes to avoid include poor time management, insufficient explanations, and not addressing all parts of a question. For example, when answering a question on local government reforms, students must not only list reforms but also explain their significance and impact.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to mark and correct past WAEC questions, identifying common errors.

Evaluation questions:
Practice questions from past WAEC papers covering all term topics.

Summary:
Effective revision and practice are essential for success in final examinations.
